computed_suggestion_rationale: The SELL-cluster branch substantially improves both Sharpe (+0.90 Sharpe points: -1.61→-0.71) and MaxDD (-2.56pp: 21.48%→18.92%), and the 467 short trades show low average per-trade loss (-0.09%), indicating the signal is broadly safe but lacks edge. The absolute Sharpe floor of 0.5 is not met (-0.712), so FLIP is not justified. REJECT is also not justified because the modified branch strictly improves on baseline across all metrics. Operator should investigate: (a) whether the BUY-cluster baseline itself has any positive-alpha regime (per-regime breakdown recommended), (b) whether the short-cluster thresholds (≥5 sellers, ≥$2M, zero-buys) are too broad and are triggering on low-signal sell clusters. A tighter dollar threshold (e.g. ≥$5M) or higher seller count (≥7) may flip the SHORT branch to positive Sharpe while keeping the safety profile.

v1_vs_v2_comparison.interpretation: The three bug fixes turned the BUY-only baseline from a money-loser into a clear winner (Sharpe 4.25 over 13 trades). Sample size is small but the trade quality (7 targets / 2 stops / 4 EOD) is consistent. The SELL branch on v2 still adds ~261 short trades that net positive (sum_pnl +0.4165, but stops outweigh targets 159 vs 74). The SELL branch's contribution drops the combined Sharpe from 4.25 to ~0, so it remains net-negative on top of a now-strong BUY baseline.

post_fix_results.computed_suggestion_v2_rationale: Acceptance criteria evaluation: (a) modified_v2_sharpe >= 0.5 → FALSE (-0.0026). (b) modified_v2_max_drawdown <= 0.20 → TRUE (0.122). (c) modified_v2_sharpe >= baseline_v2_sharpe → FALSE (the SELL branch degrades a now-very-strong baseline of 4.25 down to 0). FLIP is not justified. The bug-fix wins are concentrated in the BUY-only baseline (Sharpe 4.25) — that's where the operator should focus. The SELL branch (still gated default-OFF) currently subtracts net edge; needs threshold tightening (≥7 sellers, ≥$5M) or per-regime gating before a separate FLIP review. The big v1→v2 improvement validates the three bug fixes; the SELL branch as currently calibrated does NOT improve over the fixed baseline.

File NOT committed.

post_threshold_sweep.conclusion: NO WINNER under the strict >= 4.25 bar. Best config = C (10 sellers / $5M) at Sharpe 4.0991, MaxDD 4.21%, 12 trades, return +8.31%. Configs C and D add 7 SHORTs with a 43% stop-rate (vs 61% at the as-shipped 5/$2M), 4 targets / 3 stops — the SHORT branch at the 10-seller bar has positive edge in-sample but the 7-trade sample is thin, and total Sharpe still dips 0.15 points below baseline (4.25 -> 4.10) due to the volatility cost of the 7 extra trades. Whether doubling return (4.16% -> 8.31%) at the cost of 0.15 Sharpe is preferable is an operator preference call, not a backtest call. Recommended default: HOLD (gate stays OFF). If operator weights return / MaxDD-headroom over Sharpe-purity, Config C is the deploy candidate. No file commit per spec's 'no winner = no commit' rule.
post_threshold_sweep.path_forward: HOLD (default). Operator-overridable to FLIP-AT-CONFIG-C if return-over-Sharpe preference is stated. Do NOT pursue >= 12-seller thresholds (sample shrinks below 7 SHORTs) and do NOT run Phase 2 price-filter (spec gate not tripped).

post_cooldown_fix.bug_fixed: src/strategies/aux_data_loader.py:_recent_stop_outs queried strategy_backtest_trades unscoped — PRIOR backtest runs' stop-outs suppressed the same ticker in the CURRENT run (cross-run contamination, breaks reproducibility). The DB path was also structurally wrong: within-run trades are not persisted until run_backtest commits at the end, so the function could NEVER have observed the current run's own stops.
post_cooldown_fix.fix: Replaced the DB query with an in-memory within-run state. _per_bar_simulate now owns run_stop_history: dict[str, pd.Timestamp], updated each bar from simulate_trade exit_info when exit_reason='stop', passed into load_aux_data(..., run_stop_history=...). _recent_stop_outs is now a pure filter: drops entries outside the 21-day envelope, drops entries >= the current bar (no look-ahead). When run_stop_history is not provided (live trading via engine.py's separate load_aux_data, or any non-backtest caller), the function returns {} → cooldown becomes a no-op, matching pre-bug behavior.
post_cooldown_fix.tests: tests/strategies/test_s12_insider_sell_cluster.py 8/8 PASS post-fix (none of them inject recent_stop_outs so they're insensitive). tests/test_unified_backtest.py + test_backtest_as_of.py + test_backtest_instrument_class_dispatch.py 32/32 PASS.

post_cooldown_fix.interpretation: The cooldown bug was a Sharpe ratio funhouse mirror. Config C v2's Sharpe 4.10 was a phantom: prior runs' stops suppressed real trades and inflated the metric. v3 numbers (which are byte-stable across re-runs) reveal: (a) the BUY-only baseline is genuinely excellent (Sharpe 14.13 / MaxDD 1.16% / 9 trades). (b) The SELL branch at 5/$2M is a Sharpe-2.38 / MaxDD-9.5% addition that boosts return 7.1% → 25.9% but dilutes the BUY-only purity. (c) Tightening to 10/$5M backfires (Sharpe -1.58); the filter removed the wrong tail of clusters. (d) The structural price-confirmation filter (Phase B) is actively net-negative.
post_cooldown_fix.computed_suggestion_v3: HOLD with high confidence the SELL branch should NOT FLIP at current calibration. The BUY-only baseline (gate OFF) at Sharpe 14.13 / MaxDD 1.16% over 9 trades is the deploy candidate. The bug fix lands as a correctness fix independent of the SELL-branch decision.
post_cooldown_fix.computed_suggestion_v3_rationale: Acceptance criteria (Sharpe >= 4.25 of BUY-only baseline OR Sharpe >= 2.0 with clear downside protection): the 5/$2M config hits Sharpe 2.38 with 9.5% MaxDD — meets the 'Sharpe >= 2.0' floor but FAILS the 'protects downside' clause (it adds 9.5pp of drawdown to a baseline that draws 1.16%). Net: the SELL branch adds return at the cost of much higher drawdown and worse Sharpe vs the BUY-only baseline. No threshold sweep wins. The structural filter loses. Cooldown fix ships independently because it's a correctness fix.
